questions.prompt: Folded to the hijack at a 9-handed 100bb table. Which open is too loose?
questions.explanation: J4o has no high-card strength and no suited playability. The others are standard hijack opens.

questions.prompt: Under the gun opens to 3 big blinds. You are next with 76s and everyone else is still to act. Best default?

choices.text: Call and see a flop out of position against a strong range

questions.explanation: 76s is a later-position hand. Calling an early open while still out of position is a clear mistake.

questions.prompt: Which statement about early-position opens is right?

choices.text: Open every suited hand from under the gun.
The earlier you act, the stronger the hands you open.
Position does not change an opening range.
Under the gun should open wider than the button.

questions.explanation: More players remain and you will be out of position, so the range tightens.

questions.prompt: 100bb, middle position, folded to you with AKo. A player behind 3-bets to a normal size. What is the mistake?

choices.text: Calling and playing a flop in position

questions.explanation: AKo is ahead of a normal 3-bet range. Folding it to one raise is far too tight.
